node.author: Kacie Mischler Bass
node.metadescription: Overwhelmed by video marketing? Start small, stay authentic, and choose the right platform. Tips for creating your first business video with confidence.
node.postbody:
Deciding to incorporate video into your marketing strategy can feel very overwhelming. Where to start?

Starting to make videos can feel like a monumental task. What should the videos be about? What camera is best? How often to post? The decisions can feel overwhelming. But I'm here to tell you that starting small is the smartest way to begin. From there, you can snowball your efforts as you grow more comfortable. At the start, just focus on a few things at a time.

Begin with a simple goal

Rather than deciding you‚Äôre going to build a year-long video campaign all at once, just start with one video idea. You might choose to make an introduction to your business as your first video. Or maybe you want to answer a question you get often. Or discuss one particular product or service. Keep it small, and whatever you leave out can be addressed in future videos. If you happen to have several good ideas right away, start a list for later videos, and just focus on ONE for now.

Authenticity over perfection

Your first video is not going to be your best one. It would be pretty weird if it was! You will learn as you go, and your audience is fine with that. Don‚Äôt worry about having the perfect script, flawless takes, or humorous viral-ability. That will get better as you get used to it. Just try your best to make something useful to your audience, and the rest will follow. You have to start somewhere!

Know your platforms

You don‚Äôt need to post your video on all platforms. Know where your ideal audience congregates, and focus on that. LinkedIn is great for professionals and B2B, Facebook is handy for local customers, YouTube thrives on evergreen content that can be searched, and BlueSky is snappy and current. Choose 1-2 to start out with that you think best fits the type of person you want to reach.

Recruit some help

If it still feels like too much, or you just don‚Äôt have the time or patience to focus on video production regularly, there are so many options for production partners these days. You could find strategy help, production help, or both. Low-budget or high-budget. Annual contract or one-off. The options are nearly endless!

Companies like ours can help you post videos often and easily without much effort. We focus on the equipment and production aspects so you can stay tuned in to the content itself. But we also help with strategy and planning. It can be great to have someone hyping you up and bouncing around ideas when you‚Äôre not sure where to turn.

The important thing is just to start! Skill is built by doing, not just preparing, and done is better than perfect!

node.posttitle: The Power of Testimonials: Building Trust Through Video Content
node.postseotitle: The Power of Testimonials: Building Trust Through Video Content
node.author: Kacie Mischler Bass
node.metadescription: Build trust with your audience through video testimonials, showcasing real experiences to enhance credibility and emotional connection.
node.postbody:
In the dynamic world of business, trust is the cornerstone of successful relationships. Establishing credibility and reliability is crucial for any company striving to create a lasting impact. 

One powerful tool in achieving this is through the art of storytelling, particularly in the form of customer and employee testimonials. These authentic stories can be the key to building trust.

The Authenticity Advantage

In an era of information overload, consumers are becoming increasingly discerning. Traditional advertising methods are losing their efficacy, and people are gravitating towards authentic content that resonates with their values. Testimonials, especially when delivered through video, provide a genuine and unfiltered perspective. The sincerity in the words and emotions of a satisfied customer or dedicated employee can cut through the noise, creating a connection that goes beyond the surface level.

Humanizing the Brand

Corporate videos often run the risk of appearing sterile and detached. Testimonials inject a human element, putting a face and a story behind the brand. When potential clients can relate to the experiences of others, it humanizes the company, making it more approachable. This human touch fosters a sense of community, and people are more likely to engage with a brand they perceive as personable and relatable.

Building Credibility Through Real Experiences

Trust is earned through actions, not just words. Testimonials in video content allow real experiences to take center stage. When a customer or employee shares their positive encounters, it acts as tangible evidence of the company's commitment to delivering on its promises. This transparency builds credibility as it shows that the brand is not afraid to showcase real, unfiltered feedback, even if it includes challenges that were overcome.

Emotional Resonance

Video testimonials have a unique ability to convey emotions. A well-crafted testimonial not only communicates facts but also tugs at the heartstrings, creating an emotional resonance that is hard to achieve through other means. When an audience can connect with the emotions expressed in a testimonial, it forges a deeper connection with the brand. This emotional resonance contributes significantly to trust-building, as it goes beyond rational considerations and taps into the realm of shared human experiences.

Employee Testimonials: A Different Perspective

While customer testimonials are undoubtedly influential, the perspectives of employees can also be a potent force in building trust. Employee testimonials showcase a company's internal culture, providing insights into how the organization values and supports its team members. This transparency fosters trust not only with external stakeholders but also within the company itself, promoting a positive work environment.

In the competitive landscape of business, building and maintaining trust is paramount. Incorporating testimonials into corporate videos is a strategic approach that allows a brand to leverage the power of authentic storytelling. Whether through the lens of satisfied customers or dedicated employees, testimonials create a narrative that resonates with audiences on a personal level. This connection, rooted in sincerity and real experiences, not only builds trust but also solidifies a brand's credibility in a way that traditional marketing methods cannot. In a world where authenticity is king, testimonials in video content emerge as a formidable tool for businesses aiming to leave a lasting, positive impression.

node.postseotitle: Transform Any Video into a Compelling Story: A Step-by-Step Guide
node.author: Ben Sprangers
node.tags: Content Creation,Corporate Videos,Storytelling,Video Editing,Video Marketing,Video Production,Video Tips,Video for Business
node.metadescription: Learn how to transform any video into a compelling story with this step-by-step guide. Improve viewer engagement by crafting a cohesive narrative.
node.postbody:
Video content on its own isn‚Äôt enough to truly captivate an audience. The most successful and engaging videos tell a story, drawing viewers in and holding their attention.

Whether you‚Äôre a content creator, marketer, or video editor, knowing how to transform raw footage into a compelling narrative can dramatically enhance the impact of your videos.

This step-by-step guide will show you how to shape any video into an engaging story that resonates with your audience.

Start with a Clear Objective

Before you begin editing, determine the main message or theme of your video. What do you want the viewer to take away from this?

Whether it's to inform, entertain, or inspire, defining a clear objective will give you direction as you transform your footage into a cohesive story.

Tip: Write down your key message and keep it in mind throughout the editing process to ensure every scene supports your overall goal.

 

Organize and Review Your Footage

Once you have your objective in mind, the next step is to thoroughly review all of your raw footage. Look for the best moments that support your story and discard anything that feels repetitive or irrelevant.

Group similar clips together to create a natural flow in your narrative.

Tip: Use a video editing program to tag or color-code clips that you know will be essential to the final story. This makes it easier to spot key moments when you begin editing.

 

Craft a Narrative Structure

Every great story has a structure‚Äîbeginning, middle, and end. Video storytelling is no different. Start by introducing the context or the problem.

The middle should explore the conflict or development, and the end should offer a resolution. Whether it‚Äôs a product video, an interview, or a behind-the-scenes look, this structure ensures the video flows in a way that engages viewers.

Tip: Don‚Äôt be afraid to build tension or leave viewers curious at the beginning, as this can keep them watching until the resolution.

 

Use Transitions to Move the Story Forward

Transitions help ensure that the video moves smoothly from one part of the story to the next. Use transitions like fade-ins, fade-outs, or jump cuts to seamlessly guide viewers through different parts of your narrative.

Just make sure these transitions feel natural and aren‚Äôt distracting from the story.

Tip: Use transitions sparingly. Too many fancy transitions can make the video feel disjointed or distract from the main message.

 

Incorporate B-Roll for Visual Interest

B-roll footage, or supplementary footage, can add depth to your narrative. It can be used to illustrate key points, break up longer scenes, or show off context that the main footage doesn‚Äôt capture.

By using B-roll strategically, you keep the viewer visually engaged and help reinforce the story without relying too heavily on dialogue or narration.

Tip: Include B-roll that aligns with the story you‚Äôre telling. If you‚Äôre talking about a product, show clips of it in action to make the video more dynamic.

 

Keep Pacing in Mind

The pacing of your video is crucial for maintaining viewer engagement. Too slow, and the audience might lose interest. Too fast, and they might miss important details.

Find a balance that suits the tone of your video. If it‚Äôs educational, give viewers time to process each point. If it‚Äôs more entertainment-driven, keep the energy up with faster cuts.

Tip: Watch the video from a viewer‚Äôs perspective. If there‚Äôs a part that drags, tighten it up or consider removing it entirely.

 

Use Music and Sound to Set the Mood

Music and sound effects can greatly enhance the emotional impact of your video. Whether you need background music to set a lighthearted tone or dramatic sound effects to build tension, audio is a key element in video storytelling.

Choose tracks that complement the visuals and pacing without overpowering the narrative.

Tip: Use music sparingly and adjust the volume to ensure it enhances rather than overwhelms the dialogue or message.

 

Incorporate Dialogue and Narration Thoughtfully

If your video includes interviews, testimonials, or narration, make sure it‚Äôs aligned with the visuals and adds value to the story. Use dialogue to explain key points, but avoid overloading the viewer with information.

Narration can fill gaps in the story, but it should complement what‚Äôs happening on-screen rather than repeating it.

Tip: Write a script or outline for any narration or dialogue before recording. This will help keep the story concise and focused.

 

Add Text and Graphics to Highlight Key Points

Text and graphics can be powerful tools to emphasize important parts of your story. Use titles, lower-thirds, or captions to introduce speakers, explain concepts, or summarize important information.

Just ensure the text is clear and doesn‚Äôt distract from the visual elements of the story.

Tip: Use consistent fonts, colors, and styles to ensure the text aligns with your brand and maintains a professional look.

 

End with a Strong Call-to-Action

A compelling story should leave the viewer with a clear next step. Whether it‚Äôs visiting your website, signing up for a newsletter, or contacting your team, always include a call-to-action (CTA) at the end of your video.

This helps turn passive viewers into active participants, whether that‚Äôs making a purchase or sharing your content.

Tip: Ensure the CTA is aligned with the overall story and doesn‚Äôt feel forced. Make it feel like a natural next step in the viewer‚Äôs journey.

 

Conclusion

Creating compelling video stories is about more than just editing clips together‚Äîit‚Äôs about crafting a narrative that resonates with your audience.

By following these steps, you can transform any video footage into a cohesive, engaging story that holds your viewer‚Äôs attention and drives action.

Remember to keep your audience in mind throughout the process, and don‚Äôt be afraid to get creative with your storytelling techniques.

node.metadescription: Create engaging, effective training videos with this step-by-step guide. Boost learning with planning, visuals, interactivity, and quality production.
node.postbody:
Creating effective training videos that both engage and educate your audience is a critical skill in today‚Äôs digital landscape.

Whether you're a corporate trainer, HR professional, educator, or content creator, developing training videos that capture attention and ensure retention can significantly enhance the learning experience.

Here‚Äôs a simple, step-by-step guide to help you create training videos that hit the mark.

1. Define Clear Learning Objectives

Before you start filming, it's important to know what you want the viewer to take away from the video. Identify the key skills or knowledge the training aims to impart and make sure each part of your video reinforces these learning objectives. Keep the content focused to prevent overwhelming viewers with unnecessary information.

Tip: Write down 2-3 clear objectives to guide the structure of the video. This keeps the content focused and prevents drifting off-topic.

 

2. Plan Your Script and Visuals

Planning is key to producing effective training videos. Write a detailed script to ensure that the content flows logically and hits all of your key points. Additionally, think about how visuals will support your messaging‚Äîwhether through slides, animations, or practical demonstrations.

Tip: Break the script into short segments with clear visual or text cues to reinforce important concepts. This helps in keeping the audience engaged and aids retention.

 

3. Keep It Concise and Structured

Training videos should be concise to hold the viewer‚Äôs attention. Aim for a clear, logical structure, such as:

Introduction: Briefly explain the purpose of the training and what the viewer will learn.

Main Content: Break down complex information into bite-sized chunks.

Conclusion: Summarize key points and provide next steps for applying what was learned.

Long-winded videos may lose viewers' attention, so focus on delivering information in digestible segments.

Tip: A good length for most training videos is between 5 to 10 minutes, depending on the complexity of the topic.

 

4. Use Engaging Visuals and Examples

Visual aids are crucial for creating engaging educational videos. Use slides, diagrams, screen recordings, or even animations to reinforce the key points of your training. Real-life examples and case studies can also help ground the content in reality, making it easier for viewers to understand and apply the material.

Tip: Include visual metaphors or step-by-step demonstrations to make abstract concepts easier to grasp. Using a mix of media can also keep the video dynamic and interesting.

 

5. Prioritize Audio and Video Quality

Quality matters when it comes to creating training videos. Poor audio or video quality can be distracting and diminish the professionalism of your training content. Invest in a good microphone and ensure your lighting is suitable for clear visuals. Use a stable camera or screen recording software to capture smooth footage.

Tip: Test your audio and video equipment before shooting to ensure everything is clear and professional. A high-quality production reflects well on your brand and enhances the learning experience.

 

6. Incorporate Interactive Elements

Engaging training videos don‚Äôt have to be passive. Consider incorporating quizzes, polls, or short reflection exercises within the video to make it more interactive. This not only keeps viewers engaged but also reinforces learning by encouraging active participation.

Tip: Tools like interactive hotspots or example scenarios in videos can provide a more immersive learning experience, helping viewers apply concepts as they learn.

 

7. Use Closed Captions and Subtitles

Adding closed captions or subtitles can enhance accessibility and make it easier for viewers to follow along, especially in noisy environments or for non-native speakers. It also ensures that your content is inclusive for viewers with hearing impairments.

Tip: Many video editing platforms offer auto-captioning services, but always review them for accuracy. Adding subtitles is an easy way to boost engagement and make your content more widely accessible.

 

8. Encourage Feedback and Continuous Improvement

Once you‚Äôve created your training video, ask your audience for feedback. This can be through post-training surveys or direct responses from viewers. This feedback is invaluable for improving future videos and ensuring they meet the needs of your audience.

Tip: Include a quick survey link or feedback form at the end of the video to gather input on the video‚Äôs clarity, content, and engagement level.

 

9. Include a Clear Call-to-Action

Don‚Äôt forget to direct your audience to the next step after the training video. Whether it‚Äôs applying the learned skills, completing additional training, or accessing related resources, a clear call-to-action provides direction and purpose.

Tip: End the video by summarizing key takeaways and giving viewers a clear action to take, such as visiting a specific resource, completing a quiz, or reviewing related material.

 

10. Edit for Clarity and Flow

Finally, take the time to edit your training video for clarity and flow. Cut unnecessary footage, enhance transitions, and ensure the pacing is smooth. A well-edited video is more enjoyable to watch and helps reinforce the educational goals.

Tip: Use editing software to add highlights, annotations, or on-screen text to reinforce important points and make the content easier to follow.

 

Conclusion

Creating engaging and effective training videos doesn‚Äôt have to be complicated.

By following these best practices‚Äîplanning carefully, using engaging visuals, ensuring high-quality production, and incorporating interactive elements‚Äîyou can produce videos that not only educate but also hold the viewer‚Äôs attention.

Whether you're training employees, teaching students, or developing content for online learning, these tips will help you craft videos that make an impact.

Now that you‚Äôre equipped with these tips, it‚Äôs time to start planning your next training video!

node.metadescription: Learn 10 essential best practices for creating professional onboarding videos that engage, inform, and make a lasting impression on new employees.
node.postbody:
Onboarding new employees can be a hard process. Typically, there‚Äôs a wealth of knowledge that needs to be passed on to a new hire at any type of organization.

But overwhelming them with information, and a lack of a structured and streamlined onboarding process could set them up for failure before they even start.

Onboarding videos are a great tool to combat some of these challenges. Videos can guide new employees through the initial steps, ensuring they understand how to get going, and what they can expect.

Here are 10 tips for making a great onboarding video.

 

1. Clear Structure

An effective onboarding video introduces new employees to your company's mission, vision, and values, while also sharing its history.

Start with a warm welcome to set the tone, then move into key areas like company culture, policies, and resources.

To keep the video engaging, use visuals and graphics to separate sections and group related information together for a smoother flow.

 

2. Keep it Short and Concise

Brevity is important. Aim for a duration of 1-2 minutes per topic to maintain viewer engagement and deliver key messages effectively.

This shorter format prevents information overload and keeps the content digestible.

When onboarding new employees, concise videos make it easier for viewers to absorb and retain important information without losing interest.

Additionally, breaking up longer content into smaller sections helps ensure that each topic gets the attention it deserves.

 

3. Utilize Current Employees

A personal touch can go a long way in helping new hires feel more connected.

Be sure to include interviews or messages from leaders, employees and team members. 

This is a great way to introduce new hires to the team and make them feel welcome.

It‚Äôs also an opportunity to highlight the collaborative environment and show the human side of the company, which helps to establish trust from the start.

 

4. Use Engaging Content!

Share success stories or real-life examples that highlight your company‚Äôs values and work environment.

These stories can highlight how your team solves problems, achieves goals, or supports one another. They provide concrete examples of your company culture in action, showing new hires what makes your business unique.

Own your company personality and showcase your unique story. It‚Äôs a powerful way to make your organization stand out and to give new employees a glimpse of the team they‚Äôll be joining.

Authentic storytelling helps reinforce your values and sets the tone for their experience with the company.

 

5. Include Practical Information

Be sure to include clear instructions on essential tasks and tools.

This includes setting up email accounts, accessing company systems, or understanding reporting structures.

Testimonial videos are a powerful tool for businesses to build credibility. When done right, they go beyond marketing, serving as authentic endorsements that resonate with future customers.

However, crafting a truly impactful testimonial video requires attention to several key factors. Let‚Äôs break down the best practices that ensure your video doesn‚Äôt just connect but drives results.

 

1. Find the Right People

Not every satisfied customer will make a compelling video testimonial. You need to focus on clients who are passionate about your product or service, but also those who reflect your target audience.

Your audience needs to see themselves in the person on screen. Think about diversity too. Testimonials from clients in different industries, with varied problems, show your product‚Äôs versatility. A strong testimonial isn't just about praise, it‚Äôs about relatability and results.

 

2. Ask Simple Questions, Expect Honest Answers

Your questions guide the story, but they shouldn't feel like an interrogation.

Stick to straightforward questions: What problem were they facing? How did your solution help? What was the outcome?

Avoid yes/no questions and encourage detailed answers. Sometimes clients need time to think or expand on their experience, so be patient. A conversational style will get you the most honest responses, which translate into authentic, relatable videos.

 

3. Authenticity is Everything

There‚Äôs nothing worse than a video that feels staged. Prospects can sense when a testimonial lacks authenticity. Encourage your clients to speak naturally.

It‚Äôs fine to guide them, but resist the temptation to script their responses. The key to building trust is showing real people, talking in their own words.

Small imperfections, like a pause or laughter, humanize the client and make the testimonial more believable.

 

4. High-Quality Production Counts

Viewers are more likely to trust videos that look professional. Invest in good lighting, audio, and stable video. You don't need Hollywood-level production, but certain basics, like clear sound and steady footage, are non-negotiable.

Bad lighting or fuzzy sound can detract from the message and make even the best testimonial feel second-rate. Simple setups with a ring light and a lapel mic can drastically improve your production quality, keeping the focus on the client‚Äôs story.

 

5. Tell a Story

Your testimonial video should follow a basic narrative structure. Think of it like a mini-story.

The client introduces the problem they faced, explains how they found your product or service, and then talks about the results they experienced.

This narrative format is easy for viewers to follow and ensures the testimonial flows naturally. It turns a simple recommendation into a journey that your potential customers can relate to.

 

6. Use Real Data

Facts add weight to your testimonials. If your client mentions specific numbers‚Äîwhether it‚Äôs how much time they saved, the revenue they gained, or the efficiency boost they experienced‚Äîit will strengthen their testimonial.

Real, quantifiable results are much more persuasive than vague comments like "it worked great!" Encourage your client to include measurable outcomes where applicable to further build credibility.

 

7. Add B-Roll Footage

B-roll footage‚Äîclips that show the client using your product, interacting with their team, or demonstrating the benefits they‚Äôre discussing‚Äîhelps break up the talking head shots and adds visual interest.

It can be as simple as shots of the customer‚Äôs workspace or the product in action. B-roll can also reinforce key points without needing extra words, which can make the video feel more dynamic.

 

8. Keep It Short

Attention spans are short. The most impactful testimonial videos get to the point quickly.

Keep your video under three minutes, ideally around the one-to-two minute mark. Focus on the highlights: what was the problem, how did you solve it, and what were the results? Don‚Äôt let your client ramble.

You can always edit down for the final version, but shorter, focused videos are more likely to retain viewers and leave a lasting impression.

 

9. Stay on Brand

While the testimonial is primarily about the client, remember to subtly incorporate elements of your brand. This could be through logo placements, colors, or even background music that fits your brand‚Äôs tone.

Don‚Äôt overdo it‚Äîkeeping the client‚Äôs story at the forefront is still key‚Äîbut ensure that your branding is present to leave a professional and polished impression.

 

10. End with Action

Always give viewers a clear next step. Whether it‚Äôs visiting your website, signing up for a demo, or contacting your team, end with a call to action. This directs the momentum built by the testimonial into something actionable.

You‚Äôve shown the viewer how your product or service helped someone else‚Äînow guide them on how they can experience those same benefits.

node.postbody:
Have you ever been asked to make a video for your company and been disappointed in how it turned out? Or worse, your boss was less than thrilled with the results (and made sure you knew it)? 

Unfortunately, it‚Äôs extraordinarily easy to make a bad video if you‚Äôre not prepared, even with all of today‚Äôs technological gadgets and AI assistance. But don‚Äôt give up too fast! It‚Äôs also pretty easy to internalize some tips to make sure your future videos will impress the higher-ups every time! Just keep these tips in mind on your next shoot!

 

Planning

Any video made for a professional reason deserves to have some time spent in the planning phase, even if it‚Äôs going to be a simple social media post. Whether you need to formulate interview questions, get permissions, or scout a good shooting location, make sure you‚Äôre not scrambling to do important things the day of the shoot that should‚Äôve been done earlier. No one wants to wait for you or shoot it again later due to poor planning. High-quality videos rely on careful preparation, which is essential for effective video marketing and better content creation.

Camera

Have you ever heard the phrase, ‚ÄúThe best camera is the one you know how to use‚Äù? This is partially true, but not entirely. Just because you have a fantastic camera doesn‚Äôt mean your video will have high-quality visuals if you don‚Äôt know how to use it. If you‚Äôre fiddling with controls that you don‚Äôt fully understand, that can negatively affect your video.

Conversely, don‚Äôt rely on outdated equipment just because you‚Äôre comfortable with it. Picture quality improves continuously, so consider using a new camera or a new phone‚Äîwhatever you‚Äôre comfortable with‚Äîto ensure better video production and content creation results.

 

Focus

Relatedly, if you have a camera that allows a wide aperture, it means more light hits the sensor, but the depth of focus is smaller. A video shot out of focus is not ideal for high-quality video production, and in turn, not ideal for your company's content. Stick to a camera that has a wide focus range, or consider using a camera with reliable auto-focus features to ensure sharpness throughout your shot. Make sure you triple-check your focus before starting to ensure professional video creation.

Noise

Not everyone can or will bother with using microphones for the best sound quality, and we can accept that. But whether you do or don‚Äôt, you should think about the noises in the shooting environment. Don‚Äôt shoot somewhere with doors banging, phones ringing, or other people talking, as these can negatively impact the quality of your video. And if you do shoot with a lapel mic, make sure someone is monitoring the audio with headphones to listen for clothing interference, which is difficult to remove in post-production.

 

Light

So let‚Äôs say that you are shooting with a phone and no external microphone. I‚Äôm guessing that also means you don‚Äôt have lighting equipment. That‚Äôs fine, but you still need to consider where the light is coming from and how much there is, as proper lighting is also essential for high-quality videos. Too much light can blow out your subject and cause unfixable detail loss, while too little can result in noisy footage, negatively impacting your final video.

Further, did you know that different sources of light have different colors? Your eyes may not notice, but the camera definitely will! Don‚Äôt mix fluorescent with bulb lighting, or daylight with room lighting. Choose a location that allows your subject to face a window (never put them with their back to it) as long as the clouds aren‚Äôt coming and going. If it‚Äôs too sunny and you have curtains or thin blinds, that can work well too. If all you have are room lights, just keep the subject's face out of the shadows.

Stability

Shaky footage is the first thing to scream ‚Äúamateur‚Äù about your video. Either that or ‚Äúblockbuster action movie,‚Äù which I‚Äôm willing to bet you aren‚Äôt looking here for tips on how to make. To ensure your company's content looks polished and professional, use a tripod or a sturdy surface if you‚Äôre not able to manually hold your camera still. Video stability is key to maintaining the quality expected in your video marketing.

 

B-Roll

Capture additional footage to use as cutaways, also known as B-roll. B-roll is supplementary footage that can enhance your main video by providing visual context, illustrating points, and making transitions smoother. This extra footage helps cover up cuts and adds more supporting information to the message, making your video more dynamic and engaging.

 

Editing

There are many different editing styles out there, each suited for different types of video content. If you‚Äôre a non-editor putting this video together yourself, focus on keeping the editing snappy and straightforward. Avoid using unnecessary filters and editing gimmicks, which can distract from the message. Instead, concentrate on telling a compelling story that will keep your audience engaged from start to finish.

 

If you‚Äôre still new to creating videos, this list may seem like a lot, but it can become common sense to you if you make it a priority. Your videos deserve it!

node.postbody:
Storytelling is an essential strategy in branding. It enables you to build emotional connections and effectively communicate your brand's essence. Follow this step-by-step guide to craft compelling brand stories through video.

1. Understand Your Brand Identity

Before crafting your brand story through video production, it's crucial to have a deep understanding of your brand‚Äôs identity, values, and mission. Ask yourself:

  • What are our core values?
  • What is our mission statement?
  • What unique qualities set us apart from our competitors?

This foundation will guide you in creating compelling and authentic brand stories.

2. Know Your Audience

To create engaging video content, your story should resonate with your target audience. Understand their needs, preferences, and pain points. Conduct market research and develop detailed buyer personas to guide your storytelling efforts.

3. Define Your Story‚Äôs Purpose

Determine the primary objective of your video.

Is it to:

  • Build brand awareness?
  • Highlight a new product or service?
  • Share customer success stories?
  • Demonstrate social responsibility?

Clearly defining your purpose will ensure your video content is focused and effective.

4. Craft a Compelling Narrative

Every great story has a structure. Use the classic three-act structure to shape your video:

  • Act 1: Introduction ‚Äì Set the scene and introduce the main characters (your brand, products, or customers).
  • Act 2: Conflict ‚Äì Present a challenge or problem that resonates with your audience.
  • Act 3: Resolution ‚Äì Show how your brand provides a solution, leading to a satisfying conclusion.

This structured approach ensures your video marketing efforts are engaging and effective in conveying your message.

5. Highlight Emotion

Emotions drive decisions. In your videos, utilize storytelling techniques that evoke joy, surprise, sadness, or inspiration. By tapping into these emotional responses, you can create a deeper connection with your audience, enhancing the effectiveness of your video marketing efforts.

6. Show, Don‚Äôt Tell

Video is a powerful visual medium. Instead of merely narrating your story, use visuals to demonstrate your brand in action. This can include:

  • Footage of your products being used
  • Behind-the-scenes clips of your team
  • Real-life customer interactions

This approach enhances your video marketing by providing tangible, relatable content that resonates with your audience.

7. Incorporate Authenticity

Authenticity builds trust and credibility. Use real stories, genuine testimonials, and behind-the-scenes footage to showcase the human side of your brand. Avoid overly scripted or staged content to ensure your video production feels authentic and relatable. This authenticity will strengthen your video marketing efforts by fostering a deeper connection with your audience.

8. Use High-Quality Production

While authenticity is crucial, maintaining high production quality is equally important. Ensure your video is professionally shot and edited, paying attention to:

  • Lighting and sound quality
  • Professional editing techniques
  • High-resolution visuals

High-quality video production enhances your brand's image and ensures your video marketing efforts are impactful and engaging.

9. Include a Call to Action

End your video with a clear and compelling call to action (CTA). What do you want your viewers to do next? Whether visiting your website, following your social media channels or purchasing a product, make your CTA clear and easy to follow. This step is crucial in driving engagement and achieving your video marketing goals.

10. Distribute and Promote

Once your video is ready, distribute it across multiple channels to maximize reach:

  • Share on social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter).
  • Embed on your website and blog.
  • Include in email newsletters.
  • Use paid advertising to reach a broader audience.

Effective distribution and promotion ensure your video production efforts reach and resonate with your target audience.

Example Outline

Here‚Äôs an example outline for a brand story video:

  1. Introduction: Introduce your brand with a captivating scene or visual representing your mission.
  2. Conflict: Present a common problem or challenge that your audience faces.
  3. Resolution: Show how your product or service solves this problem.
  4. Emotional Highlight: Include a moment that evokes strong emotions, such as a customer success story.
  5. Conclusion: End with a positive resolution and a strong CTA.

Final Tips

  • Keep It Concise: Aim for a video length of 2-3 minutes to maintain viewer engagement.
  • Be Consistent: Ensure your story aligns with your overall brand messaging and visual identity.
  • Test and Optimize: Use analytics to track performance and gather feedback to improve future videos.

By following these steps, you can create compelling brand stories that resonate with your audience and effectively convey the essence of your brand through video. Happy storytelling!

Decoding the Power of Video in Social Media Engagement

The digital era has transformed how brands connect with their audience, and video content is at the heart of this revolution. Video's dynamic and versatile nature has proven to engage viewers, holding their attention longer than static images or text. By leveraging video storytelling prowess, brands can evoke emotions, share powerful messages, and foster community among social media followers.

It's not just about aesthetics; video content on social media platforms also benefits from algorithmic preferences, ensuring higher visibility and engagement rates. Understanding the nuances of social media video can be the linchpin in a successful digital marketing strategy.

Crafting Your Story: Tips for Compelling Social Media Videos

A compelling narrative is the backbone of any successful social media video. Start by identifying the core message you want to convey and wrapping it in a story that resonates with your audience. Use authentic, relatable scenarios to illustrate your points and create a personal connection. Keeping your videos concise and engaging is crucial‚Äîsocial media users have short attention spans, so they capture interest within the first few seconds.

Visuals matter. Incorporate high-quality images, consistent branding, and captions for silent viewers. Interactive elements such as polls or questions can also encourage user participation. Lastly, always include a clear call to action, guiding viewers on what steps to take next, whether visiting a website, signing up for a newsletter, or following your brand on social media.

Maximizing Reach: Best Practices for Video Distribution Across Platforms

Each social media platform has its quirks and preferred content formats. To maximize reach, tailor your videos to fit each platform's specific requirements and user behaviors. For instance, vertical videos work best on Instagram Stories and TikTok, while longer-form content may be more suitable for YouTube or Facebook.

Consistently posting content is key to keeping your audience engaged and helping your videos gain traction. Utilize scheduling tools to maintain a steady stream of content and consider the best times to post when your audience is most active. Additionally, promoting your videos through paid advertising can significantly boost their visibility to targeted segments of your audience.

Leveraging Trends and Analytics to Amplify Your Video Content

Staying on top of trends is essential for social media success. To increase relevancy and shareability, add trending hashtags, challenges, or topics to your video content. However, always ensure these trends align with your brand's image and values to maintain authenticity.

Analytics provide invaluable insights into your videos' performance. Regularly analyze view counts, watch time, engagement rates, and follower growth to understand what resonates with your audience. Use these insights to refine your content strategy, experimenting with different video formats, lengths, and narratives to discover what yields the best results.

Measuring Success: Key Metrics for Assessing Your Social Media Video Impact

The impact of your social media videos can be measured through various metrics that align with your marketing goals. Engagement metrics like likes, comments, and shares indicate how compelling your content is, while reach and impressions provide a sense of its visibility. Watch time and completion rate can help you gauge content quality and whether your storytelling hits the mark.

Conversion metrics are also critical. Track click-through rates, website traffic from videos, and conversion rates to determine the return on investment of your video content. Regularly assess these metrics to fine-tune your approach and ensure your social media videos are engaging and driving tangible business results.

As remote work becomes more prevalent, video bridges the gap between dispersed teams, fostering a sense of community and keeping everyone on the same page.

Creating Compelling Video Content for Your Team

Use storytelling techniques to create a narrative that employees can connect with, and consider including interviews, animations, or behind-the-scenes looks to add diversity to the content.

It's also important to keep videos concise and to the point to respect employees' time. Including captions and ensuring content is accessible to all team members is crucial for inclusivity.

Strategies for Implementing Video into Your Communication Plan

Incorporating video into your internal communication strategy requires careful planning. Start by determining how video will fit into the existing communication infrastructure. Choose the right platform for hosting and sharing videos, and consider the frequency and timing of video releases. It's essential to communicate the value of video to employees and encourage their participation and feedback.

Furthermore, creating a content calendar can help plan and distribute videos to complement other communication channels. Regularly reviewing and adapting the strategy based on employee engagement and feedback will ensure the content remains effective and relevant.

Measuring the Impact of Video on Employee Engagement

Key performance indicators might include video view counts, average viewing duration, and the number of comments or shares. By analyzing these metrics, companies can fine-tune their video content, format, and distribution methods to better meet the needs of their workforce and ensure that video remains a compelling and useful resource for internal communication.

Best Practices for Maintaining Privacy and Security with Internal Videos

Additionally, companies should educate employees on best practices for creating and sharing video content, including confidentiality and data protection guidelines. Regular audits and updates to security protocols can help maintain the integrity of internal videos and the trust of all employees.

Discover the immense potential of video marketing to drive business growth and stay ahead of your competitors.

Why video marketing is essential for business success

Video marketing has become an essential tool for businesses looking to succeed in today's digital landscape. With the rise of social media and the increasing popularity of video content, companies that fail to incorporate video into their marketing strategies risk being left behind. Videos have the power to convey messages in a more engaging and memorable way than text or images alone. They can capture the attention of viewers and evoke emotions, making them more likely to remember and share the content.

Additionally, video marketing allows businesses to showcase their products or services in action. By demonstrating how a product works or highlighting its benefits, companies can build trust and credibility with their audience. Videos also provide an opportunity to tell a compelling brand story, connecting with customers on a deeper level and fostering brand loyalty.

Furthermore, video marketing has the potential to reach a wider audience and increase brand visibility. With platforms like YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram offering video advertising options, businesses can target specific demographics and expand their reach. This can lead to increased website traffic, conversions, and ultimately, business growth.

In summary, video marketing is essential for business success in today's digital age. It allows companies to engage and connect with their audience, showcase their products or services, and reach a wider audience. By incorporating video into their marketing strategies, businesses can stay ahead of their competitors and drive growth.

How videos enhance brand awareness and engagement

Videos have the power to enhance brand awareness and engagement in ways that traditional marketing methods cannot. By creating compelling and shareable video content, businesses can increase their brand visibility and reach a larger audience. When viewers share videos on social media platforms, they are essentially endorsing the brand and spreading awareness to their own network of friends and followers.

Additionally, videos have the ability to evoke emotions and create a more memorable brand experience. When viewers feel emotionally connected to a brand, they are more likely to engage with the content, share it with others, and become loyal customers. This emotional connection can be achieved through storytelling, humor, or by addressing a common pain point or desire of the target audience.

Moreover, videos allow businesses to showcase their personality and values. By incorporating elements such as music, visuals, and tone of voice, companies can establish a unique brand identity that resonates with their target market. This can help differentiate them from competitors and build a loyal customer base.

In conclusion, videos enhance brand awareness and engagement by increasing brand visibility, creating emotional connections, and showcasing a brand's personality and values. By leveraging the power of video marketing, businesses can strengthen their brand image, attract a larger audience, and foster customer loyalty.

The impact of video on website traffic and SEO

Video has a significant impact on website traffic and search engine optimization (SEO). Including videos on your website can increase the time visitors spend on your site, reducing bounce rates and improving engagement metrics. This signals to search engines that your website is providing valuable content, which can positively impact your SEO rankings.

Furthermore, videos can improve your website's visibility in search engine results pages (SERPs). Google, for example, displays video thumbnails in its search results, making your website stand out and attracting more clicks. This can lead to increased organic traffic and higher click-through rates.

Additionally, videos can be optimized for SEO by incorporating relevant keywords in titles, descriptions, and tags. This helps search engines understand the content of the video and improves its chances of ranking higher in search results. Including transcripts or captions can also enhance accessibility and improve SEO by providing search engines with additional text to index.

Moreover, videos are highly shareable, which can further boost your website's visibility and traffic. When viewers share your videos on social media or other platforms, they are essentially promoting your website and driving more visitors to it.

In summary, video has a significant impact on website traffic and SEO. By including videos on your website, optimizing them for SEO, and leveraging their shareability, you can attract more visitors, improve engagement metrics, and enhance your website's visibility in search engine results.

Effective strategies for creating compelling video content

Creating compelling video content requires careful planning and execution. Here are some effective strategies to consider:

1. Know your audience: Understand who your target audience is and what type of content they are interested in. Tailor your videos to their preferences and needs.

2. Tell a story: Use storytelling techniques to create a narrative that captivates viewers and keeps them engaged. Connect with their emotions and make the content relatable.

3. Keep it concise: Attention spans are short, so aim to deliver your message in a concise and engaging way. Focus on the most important points and avoid unnecessary fluff.

4. Use visuals and audio effectively: Visuals and audio play a crucial role in capturing and retaining viewers' attention. Invest in high-quality production and editing to create a professional and visually appealing video.

5. Incorporate a call to action: Guide viewers on what to do next after watching the video. Whether it's visiting your website, subscribing to your channel, or making a purchase, a clear call to action can drive conversions.

6. Test and analyze: Continuously test different video formats, lengths, and styles to see what resonates best with your audience. Analyze metrics such as views, engagement, and conversions to measure the success of your video content and make informed improvements.

By implementing these strategies, you can create compelling video content that engages your audience, drives action, and supports your business goals.

Measuring the success of your video marketing campaigns

Measuring the success of your video marketing campaigns is crucial to understand their impact and make data-driven decisions for future strategies. Here are some key metrics to consider:

1. Views: Keep track of the number of views your videos receive. This metric provides an indication of how many people have watched your content.

2. Engagement: Measure the level of engagement with your videos, such as likes, comments, shares, and click-through rates. This indicates how well your content resonates with viewers and how likely they are to take action.

3. Conversions: Track the number of conversions that can be directly attributed to your video marketing efforts. This could include purchases, sign-ups, or downloads.

4. Reach and visibility: Monitor the reach and visibility of your videos by analyzing metrics such as impressions, reach, and click-through rates. This helps assess the effectiveness of your distribution channels and identify areas for improvement.

5. Audience retention: Analyze how long viewers are watching your videos and at what point they drop off. This can provide insights into the effectiveness of your content and help identify areas for improvement.

6. ROI: Calculate the return on investment (ROI) of your video marketing campaigns by comparing the costs incurred with the results achieved. This helps determine the overall effectiveness and profitability of your efforts.

By regularly monitoring and analyzing these metrics, you can measure the success of your video marketing campaigns, identify areas for improvement, and optimize your future strategies to achieve better results.

Discover the benefits of visual learning and how it can enhance your learning experience.

Understanding Visual Learning

Visual learning is a learning style in which information is processed and retained through visual means. It involves using visual aids such as images, videos, and diagrams to understand and remember information. This learning style is particularly effective for individuals who have a strong visual memory and prefer to see information in a visual format.

By engaging in visual learning, you can better understand complex concepts and ideas. Visual aids can help break down information into smaller, more digestible parts, making it easier to comprehend. Additionally, visual learning can help improve your overall memory retention, allowing you to recall information more easily and accurately.

Improved Retention and Comprehension

One of the main advantages of visual learning is its ability to enhance retention and comprehension. When information is presented visually, it is more likely to be remembered compared to solely reading or hearing the information. This is because visual stimuli can create stronger neural connections in the brain, leading to improved memory recall.

Visual learning also promotes better comprehension of complex concepts. By using visual aids, you can visualize abstract ideas and make connections between different pieces of information. This visual representation helps you grasp the underlying concepts more effectively, leading to a deeper understanding of the subject matter.

Enhanced Engagement and Motivation

Visual learning can significantly enhance engagement and motivation in the learning process. Watching videos or looking at visual representations can capture and maintain your attention more effectively than reading a text-heavy handbook. The dynamic nature of visual learning keeps you actively involved in the learning experience, making it more enjoyable and stimulating.

Furthermore, visual learning can boost motivation by providing a sense of accomplishment and progress. When you can visually see your understanding and mastery of a topic through diagrams or illustrations, it can inspire you to continue learning and exploring new concepts.

Effective Communication and Collaboration

Visual learning also plays a crucial role in effective communication and collaboration. When information is presented visually, it becomes easier to convey complex ideas to others. Visual aids can help break down complicated concepts into easily understandable visuals, making it simpler to communicate them to others.

In collaborative settings, visual learning promotes better teamwork and understanding among group members. Visual representations can serve as a common language that bridges communication gaps and facilitates effective collaboration. Whether it's through shared diagrams, charts, or videos, visual learning enhances group dynamics and promotes efficient knowledge sharing.

Accessibility and Flexibility

Another advantage of visual learning is its accessibility and flexibility. Videos and visual materials can be accessed anytime, anywhere, as long as you have an internet connection and a device to view them. This makes visual learning a convenient option for individuals with busy schedules or limited access to traditional learning resources.

Additionally, visual learning allows for flexibility in pacing and reviewing materials. You can pause, rewind, and rewatch videos at your own pace, ensuring that you grasp the content thoroughly. Visual aids also provide a visual reference that you can revisit whenever needed, reinforcing your understanding of the topic.

Discover effective tips and tricks for mastering workplace communication and enhancing productivity.

Understanding the Importance of Workplace Communication

Effective workplace communication is essential for the success and productivity of any organization. It allows employees to stay informed and up to date on important company news and announcements. Communication helps to build trust and transparency, fosters collaboration and teamwork, and ensures that everyone is working towards common goals. Without effective communication, misunderstandings can occur, leading to conflicts, delays, and decreased productivity. Therefore, it is crucial for employees to understand the importance of workplace communication and actively strive to improve their communication skills.

Developing Clear and Concise Communication Skills

Clear and concise communication is key to avoid misunderstandings and ensure that messages are delivered accurately. To develop clear and concise communication skills, it is important to use simple and straightforward language, avoid jargon and technical terms whenever possible, and focus on the main points of your message. Additionally, active listening is essential for effective communication. This means giving your full attention to the speaker, asking clarifying questions, and paraphrasing to ensure understanding. By honing these skills, employees can improve their ability to communicate clearly and concisely, leading to better collaboration and productivity in the workplace.

Leveraging Technology for Efficient Communication

In today's digital age, technology plays a crucial role in workplace communication. There are numerous tools and platforms available that can streamline communication processes and improve efficiency. For example, email allows for quick and convenient written communication, while instant messaging apps enable real-time conversations and quick decision-making. Video conferencing tools facilitate face-to-face communication, even when employees are geographically dispersed. By leveraging technology effectively, organizations can overcome communication barriers, enhance collaboration, and ensure that information is shared in a timely and efficient manner.

Building Strong Interpersonal Relationships

Strong interpersonal relationships are the foundation of effective workplace communication. When employees have positive relationships with their colleagues, they are more likely to communicate openly, trust each other, and collaborate effectively. To build strong interpersonal relationships, it is important to foster a supportive and inclusive work environment, encourage open and honest communication, and promote teamwork and collaboration. Regular team-building activities and social events can also help strengthen relationships and create a sense of camaraderie among employees. By investing in building strong interpersonal relationships, organizations can create a positive and productive work culture.

Effective Communication in Remote Work Environments

With the rise of remote work, effective communication in virtual settings has become increasingly important. Remote employees rely heavily on digital communication tools to stay connected with their colleagues and managers. It is crucial to establish clear communication channels and protocols to ensure that remote workers have access to the information they need and can collaborate effectively with their team members. Regular check-ins, virtual meetings, and collaborative project management tools can help bridge the communication gap in remote work environments. By prioritizing effective communication in remote settings, organizations can maintain productivity and foster a sense of belonging among remote employees.

node.postbody:
Town hall live-stream events are an excellent opportunity to engage with your audience and create unique content. However, figuring out how to turn a live event into content that resonates with your audience can take time and effort. In this blog post, we will discuss three ways to drive content from a town hall live-stream event.

1. Use Q&A Sessions as Inspiration

One of the most valuable aspects of a town hall live-stream event is the Q&A session. Your audience's questions can provide valuable insights into what they are interested in and care about. Use these questions as inspiration for future content. For example, if many people ask about a specific topic, you could create a blog post or video addressing that topic in more detail. Alternatively, create a social media post or infographic summarizing the key takeaways from the Q&A session.

2. Repurpose Video Footage

The video footage from your town hall live-stream event can be repurposed in various ways. For example, you could create shorter clips highlighting key event moments. These clips can be shared on social media or included in future blog posts or articles. You could also create a highlight reel that showcases the best moments from the event.

3. Use Attendee Feedback to Enhance Your Content

After your town hall live-stream event, gather feedback from attendees.  This feedback can be incredibly valuable in helping you create content that resonates with your audience.  Use the feedback you receive to inform future content.  For example, if many people would like more information on a specific topic, you could create a blog post or video that delves deeper into that topic.

Conclusion

Driving content from a town hall livestream event can initially seem daunting. With a bit of creativity, it can be a great way to engage with your audience and create unique content. By using Q&A sessions as inspiration, repurposing video footage, and using attendee feedback to enhance your content, you can create content that resonates with your audience and helps to establish your brand as an authority in your industry.

It has become a popular way for individuals and businesses to connect with their audiences and share their experiences, events, and products more authentically and engagingly. Here are some things marketers should know about live streaming:

  1. It allows for real-time interaction: A main benefit of live streaming is that it allows for real-time interaction between the broadcaster and the audience. Viewers can ask questions and comment in the chat, and the host can respond in real-time, creating a sense of community and connection. Especially useful for product demonstrations, Q&A sessions, and other interactive content.

  2. It can be more engaging: Live streams can be more engaging than pre-recorded videos because they offer a sense of exclusivity and immediacy. Viewers know they are watching something happening right now, which can make them feel more connected to the content and the broadcaster.

  3. It requires good planning and execution: While live streams can be spontaneous and unscripted, they still need good planning and execution to be successful. A precise idea of what you want to achieve with your live stream and a plan for how you will execute it is essential. You need to choose the right platform, set up the necessary equipment, and promote the live stream in advance.

  4. It's crucial to have good audio and video quality: Poor audio and video quality can distract from the content of the live stream and turn off viewers. Investing in good equipment and ensuring that the lighting and audio are well-balanced is essential to maintaining the quality of your brand, or better yet, consider outsourcing to a reputable video production company to handle the production of your live stream event.

Here are some tips on how to use popular video trends for corporate videos:

 

Choose trends that fit your brand

Not all social media video trends will be a good fit for your business. Look for trends that align with your brand's values and image. For example, if you're a luxury fashion brand, your videos should probably have a different feel than a company that sells toys (like Lego, shown above).

 

Use animation and motion graphics

Modern videos harness the power of creative visuals, and animation and motion graphics can be a great way to bring your corporate message to life (ex: Evian). Whether you're explaining a complex concept or simply highlighting the benefits of your product or service, animation and motion graphics can help to make your video more engaging and easy to understand.

 

Include user-generated content

User-generated content, such as testimonials or reviews from customers, can add authenticity and credibility to your corporate videos. Leverage the power of storytelling

node.postbody:
Livestreaming lets you broadcast online in real time using an easily accessible public or private platform such as Facebook Live, along with a camera and an internet connection. The uses for livestreaming are varied, so it's important to find out what your audience would be interested in watching, and flesh it out with engaging, dynamic content. Some ideas could include product/service demos, Q and A's, interviews, training, educational speeches, and more.

Remember, it is a live event, so make sure you take advantage of it by getting your viewers involved and interacting with them. Viewer interaction guarantees engagement, helping you build better relationships and giving your audience something they can‚Äôt get from pre-recorded video. Here‚Äôs what makes livestreaming so great.  

Setup Flexibility

Livestreaming can be as simple or complex as you want it to be. At the most basic level, you just need a device with a camera and an internet connection, while a more advanced setup could involve multiple cameras and a camera switcher to control the action. With livestreaming, you can decide what works best to reach your audience while also meeting your budgetary requirements. 

Pre-event Marketing

You should build up your live event as a can‚Äôt-miss opportunity by marketing it to your target audience. Ask them what they would like to see. Offer them a gift if they register early. Make your audience feel like they will be missing out on something special if they don't attend, so creating a sense of urgency to tune in and watch is a major priority. 

Giveaways

To aid in the marketing of your company and your livestream, it‚Äôs a great idea to give something away. That doesn‚Äôt necessarily mean a free product or service, but offer your attendees a free white paper if they sign up for your newsletter. You could also send out show notes or a powerpoint of your presentation, just for attending your event. 

Audience Interaction

Another huge benefit of livestreaming is audience interaction. Give them the ability to ask questions or post comments. Respond to those questions during the event to really draw people in. Not only does it allow the audience to get answers they might not otherwise have gotten, but it helps build trust with your company.  

Post-event Follow-up

Another major benefit to livestreaming is the ability to follow-up after the event. If some audience questions didn‚Äôt get answered, send them a response. Send out a survey asking for input. This will allow you to tailor future events to what your audience is looking for. It can also allow you to pinpoint what might not be working with your livestream. Maybe they liked that you had a product demonstration but not how it was shown. Post-event surveys are key to tailor your message to reach your audience better next time. 

Post-event Content

Even though it is a live event, recording it is a good idea to use as future content. Take snippets of your livestream and put those out on social media channels. This allows you to get the best of both worlds. The livestream is geared towards people that already like your business while the snippets you take from the livestream can allow you to reach a wider audience and pull in new customers. 

On-Site Studios Integration

We can also put names and titles on screen, play videos, display pictures, and more. It‚Äôs even possible to have multiple people onscreen, even if they're not in the same location.. node.posttitle: Tips for Conducting Great Interviews
node.postseotitle: Interviewing Techniques for Success | On-Site Studios Tips for Videos
node.author: Hau Khuong
node.metadescription: Being good at conducting interviews is an important part in creating a profile with great content.
node.postbody:
Profile-style videos are one of the most common types of corporate video, and being good at conducting interviews is an important part in creating a profile with great content.

Here at On-Site Studios, you always have the option of having our team ask the questions or to pose the questions yourself. Here are a couple of tips you can use to get great answers if you choose to conduct the interview yourself.

Positioning

You should position yourself next to the cart/camera so that the onscreen talent can look right at you and be at a profile angle to the lens. Work with your producer to make sure you are correctly positioned for the talent's lighting.

Make Sure the Interviewee is Comfortable

As the interviewer, you set the tone. You don‚Äôt want to make the interviewee feel uncomfortable.

Go over the interview process with them before beginning. Start off with some simple questions to ease into the interview. Don‚Äôt go straight into the ‚Äúhard-hitting" questions.

You can make the interview conversational, like you are having a normal chat. However, be sure you are not interrupting the person as they are answering, to ensure that there are clean sound bites. Give them a couple of seconds after they finish before moving on to the next question.  

Two is Better Than One!

During the interview, it is always good to have more than one take of each answer. The second take doesn‚Äôt have to be the same as the first take. In fact, in some cases, the second one is unexpectedly better than the first.

Be Encouraging

It‚Äôs hard being in front of a camera sometimes! If the interviewee is struggling, be encouraging! Let them know they can take as many tries as they need to, and if necessary, they can always come back to the question later.

Have Them Rephrase the Question in Their Answer

Keep in mind, usually the interviewer's voice won‚Äôt be in the video, and the viewer will not hear the question. That means that answers should rephrase the question and be complete sentences to give context.

For example, they could answer "I went to medical school for eight years," instead of answering "eight."

Evergreen Content 

Your videos should be able to stay relevant for a long time! Sometimes an answer cannot be used in the video because it is "time stamped."

For example, an answer such as "I've been working here for three years" will be outdated the following year. Find ways to rephrase it so that the information stays relevant no matter when the viewer sees it.

As always, On-Site Studios is here to help you if you have any questions about interviewing.

node.posttitle: The Ultimate Dictionary of Video Jargon : Understanding The Language
node.postseotitle: Video Jargon Dictionary | On-Site Studios - Understand Video Terms
node.author: Kacie Mischler Bass
node.metadescription: When working with a video production company, there is jargon you will have to know. Here are definitions to some common video terms.
node.postbody:
As in all industries, video production uses phrases and jargon that may not be initially familiar to outsiders. If you're interacting with a producer, editor, animator, or video sales team member and they use a term you don't recognize, you are not alone! 

Here are some terms and meanings that video studios use regularly:

Animation: Visuals made completely with computer programs - videos can have some, all, or no animation

B-roll: Clips and images recorded by the studio, provided by clients, or supplied by stock sites that help illustrate the topic visually

Bug: A small logo placed in a corner that remains visible throughout the video

Cross Dissolve/Fade: A video-editing technique that involves gradually fading up the start of a new clip over the end of the previous one

CTA: Stands for Call To Action; a written or spoken phrase that inspires the viewer to take a desired next step (example: "Visit us online at...")

End Tag: The ending slide that contains some combination of logo, contact information, or call to action to wrap up the video

IFB: The earpiece worn by on-air talent allowing them to discretely hear instructions from the production team

Jump Cut: A video-editing technique that involves a cut between two clips of the same angle, in which the on-screen talent appears to jump position

Keying/Keyed Footage: Keying is the process of removing the green background from the footage so that a different background can be added in post-production

Livestream: To broadcast the video simultaneously while it is being recorded, allowing for interaction with the audience if desired

Lower Third: A text graphic that appears towards the bottom of the screen that displays additional information such as talent names, credentials, definitions, or acronyms, etc.

Pan: A camera movement that involves swiveling the camera horizontally from a fixed point (from the word panorama) - not to be confused with tilt, which is the vertical equivalent

Profile: A term for positioning the talent; not speaking directly to the camera, but rather sitting at an angle with gaze offscreen

Punch in: A video-editing technique that involves cropping closer than the original composition in order to avoid the look of jump cuts or to add variety

Raw Footage: Unedited footage, straight out of the camera

Supers: Collective term for text or graphics superimposed over video footage

Talent: The person/people appearing onscreen

Voiceover/VO: Narration audio that plays over separate visuals
